_what_this_is: The FROZEN retrieval protocol for the cross-disease endpoint corpus behind research/manuscripts/endpoint-corpus.json and the manuscript it feeds. It is committed BEFORE any fetch runs. That ordering is the whole point: query choice is the only discretion left once the corpus rule forbids disease-level selection, so freezing the queries in advance is what stops the corpus from being assembled to fit the thesis.

_the_corpus_rule.unit: one arm of one interventional trial in a solid tumour.
_the_corpus_rule.no_disease_filter: NO tumour type, grade, rarity or indolence descriptor is used as an inclusion criterion anywhere in this protocol. Every query below selects on a DESIGN FEATURE (a control arm, a four-cell best-response table, a named response criterion). Disease identity is recorded as an attribute and used only for post-hoc description. Round 3 is the single deliberate exception and is not an arm-selection round: it retrieves the response-criteria and consensus documents themselves, which are disease-named by their nature, and it contributes ZERO arms to the corpus.
_the_corpus_rule.extraction_eligibility: an arm enters the re-read numerator only if the report prints all four best-response cells (CR, PR, SD, PD) as integers with the evaluable denominator. Counts are never reconstructed from percentages (POLICY-evidence 2.1). Arms failing this stay in the denominator with disposition four_cell_incomplete.
_the_corpus_rule.control_arm_eligibility: additionally, the arm received no active anti-tumour agent under test (placebo, best supportive care, or observation) and the figure quoted is pre-crossover.
_the_corpus_rule.dispositions: every screened record carries a disposition, included or not. The excluded set is the audit trail and is simultaneously the reporting census.

_date_window.from: no lower bound -- response criteria predate RECIST and the audit needs them
_date_window.to: 2026-08-09, the day this protocol was frozen
_date_window.why_no_lower_bound: a lower bound would silently drop the older criteria documents that the prior-art audit exists to find, and would bias the reporting census toward modern practice.

_method: Three rounds, all through .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml in URL-manifest mode. Round 1 retrieves control/placebo/BSC/observation arms. Round 2 retrieves arms printing a four-cell best-response table. Round 3 retrieves the response-criteria and consensus documents for the prior-art audit, every one of them as a TITLE search so that no identifier in this repository is written from recollection -- PMIDs and DOIs come back FROM the fetch and are recorded afterwards in _identifiers_returned_by_these_fetches.

_deferred_round_4.what: per-disease accruable-n from ClinicalTrials.gov ACTUAL enrolment.
_deferred_round_4.why_deferred: the accrual axis is measured only for diseases that actually appear in the corpus. Querying accrual per disease before knowing which diseases landed would reintroduce disease-level selection through the back door.
_deferred_round_4.rule_when_it_runs: completed interventional trials only; EnrollmentType ACTUAL only, never ESTIMATED; terminated-for-accrual trials retained and flagged rather than dropped.
_deferred_round_4.status: RUN 2026-08-09. Abstracts were measured first and do not carry the four cells: of 1277 unique abstracts screened across rounds 1-2, four labelled categories appeared in 5 and only 1 had a denominator they summed to. That is a reporting finding, not a retrieval failure, and it is why the four-cell corpus is taken from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results instead -- where per-category participant counts are a structured field rather than a sentence. Year buckets partition the pull because the API pages by token and a static URL manifest cannot follow one; buckets are administrative and disease-neutral, so they introduce no selection.

_dispatch: .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml with targets_json=<the round object with underscore keys stripped>, targets_mode=replace, slug=<the round's slug>, ref=<the working branch>. One dispatch per round; distinct slugs get distinct concurrency groups and run in parallel. NOTE: this workflow's `query` input has a non-empty default, so a targets_json dispatch runs the URL path ONLY and never the Europe PMC search path.
_a_key_here_is_a_filename_not_a_result: A name in this file records what was ASKED FOR. Whether the fetch succeeded, and with what HTTP status, is in each round's _manifest.json on the literature-cache branch. Read the manifest, never this file, for what was actually retrieved.
_clinicaltrials_gov_transport_warning: ClinicalTrials.gov payloads cached before 2026-08-07 were silently damaged: strip_html() ran over JSON and deleted whole modules between literal angle brackets. lit_fetch_urls.py now routes structured payloads to disk verbatim via _looks_structured(). Any CT.gov record quoted from this corpus must come from a fetch dated after that fix.

_rounds.xdisease-control-arms: round 1 -- control, placebo, BSC and observation arms
_rounds.xdisease-fourcell: round 2 -- arms printing a four-cell best-response table
_rounds.xdisease-ctg-results: round 4 -- ClinicalTrials.gov POSTED RESULTS (the four-cell tables) and the accrual axis

_identifiers_returned_by_these_fetches._why_this_block_exists: lint_citations.py requires every identifier appearing in prose to be anchored in a tracked .json. This block is filled in AFTER the fetches land, from the returned records, and never from recollection. It is empty until then, and that is correct.

round4_xdisease-ctg-results._why: flat {name: url} map, so fetch-literature.yml can take it via targets_file instead of an inline dispatch payload
